comment: Loading and the CLI's download take the same names in every runtime, so the
vocabulary that turns those names into languages has to mean one thing everywhere.
Three implementations of it exist — catalog::expand_bundles in Rust,
expandBundles in JavaScript, and Lumis.Languages.expand_bundles in Elixir —
and nothing else pins them to each other.
Expected values are expressed as relationships rather than literal language
lists, so adding a language to a bundle does not require editing this file
and a divergence is still a failure.

spellings.comment: Every spelling in a group names one bundle, so all expand identically.

passthrough.comment: Expansion resolves bundles, it does not validate languages, so an unknown language survives it and fails later where the error can say why.

deduplication.comment: A bundle followed by one of its own members yields that member once. Adjacent-only dedup would keep both.

ordering.comment: Names keep the order they were given, with bundle members spliced in place.

unknownBundles.comment: A `bundle-` prefixed name that names no bundle is an error, never a language name to look up.

store.comment: What `cache` leaves behind, and what `load` therefore also leaves behind. Globs, because parser files are content-addressed.
